summary: Low occupancy and dependency stalls prevent saturation of compute and memory resources.
reasoning: Compute SOL is 41.47% and memory SOL is 51.68%, both below 60%. DRAM throughput is only 6.92%, with a 97.38% L2 hit rate, so external-memory bandwidth is not the limiting factor.

root_causes.cause: Shared-memory allocation restricts resident blocks and reduces latency-hiding capacity.

evidence.interpretation: Each block allocates approximately 37 KB of shared memory.
Shared memory limits residency to two blocks per SM, versus eight allowed by registers.
Low achieved occupancy leaves few warps available to hide execution latency.

fixes.fix: Autotune BLOCK_N, including 32 versus the current 64, to reduce shared-memory allocation and increase resident blocks.
fixes.rationale: Higher residency can improve latency hiding; benchmark the trade-off against additional loop iterations and smaller dot products.

root_causes.cause: The repeated dot–softmax–dot sequence exposes short-latency dependencies and synchronization overhead.

evidence.interpretation: Short-scoreboard waits are substantial, consistent with shared-memory or other short-latency producer-consumer dependencies.
Barrier waits further reduce instruction-issue opportunities.

fixes.fix: Test software pipelining of the key-block loop using tl.range with num_stages=2 to overlap upcoming K/V loads with current-block computation.
fixes.rationale: Overlapping independent loads can reduce exposed dependency latency; retain the change only if its extra shared-memory usage does not worsen occupancy.
